attacks.claim: The run-cost estimate is off by about 30x. 2.28B input tokens is one day of logs (38M lines/day), but it is priced as the monthly figure. Over 30 days that is about 68B tokens, roughly $34K/month at $0.50/1M, far above the $1,500 budget. Output is likewise per-day (~$207/month, not ~$7).
attacks.evidence: "Input: 38M lines x 60 tokens = 2.28B tokens -> ~$1,140" and "Estimated total: ~$1,150/month, within the $1,500 budget."

attacks.claim: Spend is unbounded. Every service is summarized every 5 minutes with no token cap, sampling, budget alarm, circuit breaker, or skip rule for quiet windows. Peak-day volume (61M lines, 1.6x average) and incident log storms scale cost linearly with nothing to stop it, and the plan has no headroom.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any token/spend ceiling, usage alerting, sampling or per-window cap; "sends the last 5 minutes of logs per service to the LLM"; "peak day 61M"

attacks.claim: The staffing math ignores the stated on-call load. Both engineers are assumed to deliver 12 eng-weeks full-time while on-call/interrupt work averages 50% of their time, leaving about 6 eng-weeks of capacity against a 12 eng-week estimate with no buffer. The plan also does not say who covers on-call during the build or who owns the new system afterward.
attacks.evidence: "Staffing: both platform engineers full-time for 6 weeks (2 x 6 = 12 eng-weeks)." vs. context "on-call/interrupt work averages 50% of their time"

attacks.claim: Every application log line is sent to an external LLM vendor, relying on a redaction stage that only names emails, tokens, card numbers and IPs. User/customer IDs, names, tenant IDs, free-text payloads and other secrets are not covered. The Q1 audit was for the retention policy, not third-party egress. There is no minimization (error/anomaly-only forwarding) and no check that new log fields or services cannot bypass redaction.
attacks.evidence: "already masks emails, tokens, card numbers and IPs for our log retention policy (audited in Q1)"; "forwards every application log line to the summarizer queue"

attacks.claim: The plan does not show that the DPA and customer contracts cover sending customer-originated log content to a new AI sub-processor. Corvid's processing region/cross-border transfer, sub-processor disclosure or notice to customers, and retention/access for new copies of the data (Redis queue, Postgres summaries, eval replay) are all unaddressed.
attacks.evidence: "Corvid account has zero-retention enabled; data processing addendum signed by Legal (ref DPA-0417)." ABSENT: processing region, sub-processor/customer notice, retention for summaries and queued data

attacks.claim: Log lines are untrusted, attacker-influenceable text fed into an LLM prompt, and the output is posted into PagerDuty for responders acting under pressure. The plan defines no prompt-injection defenses or output validation/sanitization.
attacks.evidence: "sends the last 5 minutes of logs per service to the LLM with a fixed prompt and stores a structured summary"

attacks.claim: There are no failure-mode, observability or kill-switch provisions. The plan specifies no timeout/retry/backoff when Corvid is slow or down, no backlog handling for the queue, no staleness/health alerting on the summarizer, no handling of PagerDuty or service-catalog failures, and no feature flag or rollback for log-tap, which sits on the live Vector pipeline.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: timeout/retry/circuit breaker, staleness alerting, queue sizing/backpressure, feature flag or rollback; "log-tap (new): subscribes to the existing Vector pipeline"

attacks.claim: The design cannot deliver several promised outputs. 'Within seconds of a page' conflicts with precomputed 5-minute summaries that can be stale. 'New error signatures' needs a baseline although input is only the last 5 minutes. 'Suspected deploy' has no deploy-event input source.
attacks.evidence: "every 5 minutes, sends the last 5 minutes of logs per service"; "new error signatures, affected endpoints, suspected deploy"; ABSENT: deploy/change-event source or history baseline

attacks.claim: The evaluation does not validate the goal. The incident commander grades retrospectively instead of the on-call responders who use the summary at page time. A 5% misleading allowance (at most 2 of 40) is a coarse gate for a tool read mid-incident. There is no baseline of where the 47 min MTTR goes, no adoption metric, and a quarterly median MTTR is noisy for a low incident count.
attacks.evidence: "have the incident commander grade it (useful / partially / misleading). Launch gate: >= 70% useful, <= 5% misleading."; "Target: median MTTR 47 min -> 30 min within one quarter of launch."

attacks.claim: Throughput and storage are not sized: no queue capacity, consumer concurrency, LLM rate limits, or retention/TTL for summaries and queued lines on shared Redis/Postgres. Per-window input is also uncapped and could exceed model context.
attacks.evidence: "Queue + storage: existing Redis and Postgres, negligible."; ABSENT: queue sizing, TTL, per-window token cap

attacks.claim: The plan hard-wires a single external vendor with no provider abstraction, fallback, or exit path.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: provider abstraction or alternate/self-hosted model; "Model: Corvid-mini"
